title: sql_cacher Module
content_markdown: The sql_cacher module introduces the possibility to cache data from a SQL-based database (using different OpenSIPS modules which implement the DB API) into a cache system implemented in OpenSIPS through the CacheDB Interface. This is done by specifying the databases URLs, SQL table to be used, desired columns to be cached and other details in the OpenSIPS configuration script.
overview: The sql_cacher module introduces the possibility to cache data from a SQL-based database (using different OpenSIPS modules which implement the DB API) into a cache system implemented in OpenSIPS through the CacheDB Interface. This is done by specifying the databases URLs, SQL table to be used, desired columns to be cached and other details in the OpenSIPS configuration script.
how_it_works:
The cached data is available in the script through the read-only pseudovariable “$sql_cached_value” similar to a Key-Value system. A specified column from the SQL table has the role of “key” therefore the value of this column along with the name of a required column are provided as "parameters" to the pseudovariable returning the appropriate value of the column.

There are two types of caching available:

*   _full caching_ - the entire SQL table (all the rows) is loaded into the cache at OpenSIPS startup;
    
*   _on demand_ - the rows of the SQL table are loaded at runtime when appropriate keys are requested.
    

For on demand caching, the stored values have a configurable expire period after which they are permanently removed unless an MI reload function is called for a specific key. In the case of full caching the data is automatically reloaded at a configurable interval. Consequently if the data in the SQL database changes and a MI reload function is called, the old data remains in cache only until it expires.

dependencies_required.name: The OpenSIPS modules that offer actual database back-end connection
dependencies_required.reason: must be loaded before this module

exported_parameters.name: cache_table
exported_parameters.description: This parameter can be set multiple times in order to cache multiple SQL tables or even the same table but with a different configuration. The module distinguishes those different entries by an “id” string. The caching entry is specified via this parameter that has it's own subparameters. Each of those parameters are separated by a delimiter configured by [spec_delimiter](#param_spec_delimiter "1.3.2.�spec_delimiter (string)") and have the following format: _param_name=param_value_ The parameters are: * _id_ : cache entry id * _db_url_ : the URL of the SQL database * _cachedb_url_ : the URL of the CacheDB database * _table_ : SQL database table name * _key_ : SQL database column name of the “key” column * _key_type_ : data type for the SQL "key" column: * string * int If not present, default value is “string” * _columns_ : names of the columns to be cached from the SQL database, separated by a delimiter configured by [columns_delimiter](#param_columns_delimiter "1.3.4.�columns_delimiter (string)"). If not present, all the columns from the table will be cached * _on_demand_ : specifies the type of caching: * 0 : full caching * 1 : on demand If not present, default value is “0” * _expire_ : expire period for the values stored in the cache for the on demand caching type in seconds If not present, default value is “1 hour” The parameters must be given in the exact order specified above. Overall, the parameter does not have a default value, it must be set at least once in order to cache any table.
exported_parameters.example_value:
id=caching_name
db_url=mysql://root:opensips@localhost/opensips_2_2
cachedb_url=mongodb:mycluster://127.0.0.1:27017/db.col
table=table_name
key=column_name_0
columns=column_name_1 column_name_2 column_name_3
on_demand=0
exported_parameters.example_code:
modparam("sql_cacher", "cache_table", "id=caching_name
db_url=mysql://root:opensips@localhost/opensips_2_2
cachedb_url=mongodb:mycluster://127.0.0.1:27017/db.col
table=table_name
key=column_name_0
columns=column_name_1 column_name_2 column_name_3
on_demand=0")
exported_parameters.notes: The parameters must be given in the exact order specified above.

exported_parameters.name: spec_delimiter
exported_parameters.description: The delimiter to be used in the caching entry specification provided in the _cache_table_ parameter to separate the subparameters. It must be a single character.
exported_parameters.notes: It must be a single character.

exported_parameters.name: pvar_delimiter
exported_parameters.description: The delimiter to be used in the “$sql_cached_value” pseudovariable to separate the caching id, the desired column name and the value of the key. It must be a single character.
exported_parameters.notes: It must be a single character.

exported_parameters.name: columns_delimiter
exported_parameters.description: The delimiter to be used in the _columns_ subparameter of the caching entry specification provided in the _cache_table_ parameter to separate the desired columns names. It must be a single character.
exported_parameters.notes: It must be a single character.

exported_parameters.name: sql_fetch_nr_rows
exported_parameters.description: The number of rows to be fetched into OpenSIPS private memory in one chunk from the SQL database driver. When querying large tables, adjust this parameter accordingly to avoid the filling of OpenSIPS private memory.

exported_parameters.name: full_caching_expire
exported_parameters.description: Expire period for the values stored in cache for the full caching type in seconds. This is the longest time that deleted or modified data remains in cache.

exported_parameters.name: reload_interval
exported_parameters.description: This parameter represents how many seconds before the data expires (for full caching) the automatic reloading is triggered.

exported_mi_functions.name: sql_cacher_reload

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: the specific key to be reloaded.

exported_mi_functions.description:
Reloads the entire SQL table in cache or the single key (if key provided) in _full caching_ mode.

Reloads the given key or invalidates all the keys in cache in _on demand_ mode.

exported_pseudo_variables.name: $sql_cached_value(id{sep}col{sep}key)
exported_pseudo_variables.description:
The cached data is available through this read-only PV.The format is the following:

*   _sep_ : separator configured by [pvar_delimiter](#param_pvar_delimiter "1.3.3.�pvar_delimiter (string)")
    
*   _id_ : cache entry id
    
*   _col_ : name of the required column
    
*   _key_ : value of the “key” column
    
**Example�1.9.�`sql_cached_value(id{sep}col{sep}key) pseudo-variable` usage**

...
$avp(a) = $sql_cached_value(caching_name:column_name_1:key1);
...

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.1. cache_table parameter usage
configuration_examples.description: Demonstrates how to set the cache_table parameter with various subparameters like id, db_url, cachedb_url, table, key, columns, and on_demand.
configuration_examples.code:
modparam("sql\_cacher", "cache\_table",
"id=caching\_name
db\_url=mysql://root:opensips@localhost/opensips\_2\_2
cachedb\_url=mongodb:mycluster://127.0.0.1:27017/db.col
table=table\_name
key=column\_name\_0
columns=column\_name\_1 column\_name\_2 column\_name\_3
on\_demand=0")
configuration_examples.explanation: The parameters must be given in the exact order specified above.

configuration_examples.description: Shows how to configure the delimiter used to separate subparameters in the cache_table parameter.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.3. pvar_delimiter parameter usage
configuration_examples.description: Shows how to configure the delimiter used in the $sql_cached_value pseudovariable.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.4. columns_delimiter parameter usage
configuration_examples.description: Shows how to configure the delimiter used to separate column names in the columns subparameter.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.5. sql_fetch_nr_rows parameter usage
configuration_examples.description: Shows how to set the number of rows fetched into private memory in one chunk.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.6. full_caching_expire parameter usage

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.7. reload_interval parameter usage

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.8. sql_cacher_reload usage
configuration_examples.description: Demonstrates the use of the MI function to reload cached data.
configuration_examples.code:
...
$ opensips-cli -x mi sql\_cacher\_reload subs\_caching
...
$ opensips-cli -x mi sql\_cacher\_reload subs\_caching alice@domain.com
...
configuration_examples.explanation: Reloads the entire SQL table in cache or the single key (if key provided) in full caching mode. Reloads the given key or invalidates all the keys in cache in on demand mode.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.10. Example database content - carrierfailureroute table
configuration_examples.description: Shows the structure and content of a sample SQL table to be cached.
configuration_examples.explanation: Suppose one in interested in caching the columns: “host_name”, “reply_code”, “flags” and “next_domain” from the “carrierfailureroute” table of the OpenSIPS database.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.11. Setting the cache_table parameter
configuration_examples.description: Provides a specific configuration for caching the carrierfailureroute table.
configuration_examples.code:
modparam("sql\_cacher", "cache\_table",
"id=carrier\_fr\_caching
db\_url=mysql://root:opensips@localhost/opensips
cachedb\_url=mongodb:mycluster://127.0.0.1:27017/my\_db.col
table=carrierfailureroute
key=id
columns=host\_name reply\_code flags next\_domain")
configuration_examples.explanation: In the first place, the details of the caching must be provided by setting the module parameter “cache_table” in the OpenSIPS configuration script.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.12. Accessing cached values
configuration_examples.description: Shows how to retrieve values from the cached carrierfailureroute table in the script.
configuration_examples.explanation: Next, the values of the cached columns ca be accessed through the “$sql_cached_value” PV.
